advances: Identifies exactly where the endpoint-only depth equals \(m\), by reflected containment in \(A_0\) itself. If this region is nonempty, every attained balanced active triple in a counterexample has exactly one row with endpoint payment \(m\); that row has a bisected full middle chord and admits an exact finite tail representative. At least one of the other two rows has an off-center full middle chord. This restricts the displaced-chord case without proving the locked target. An explicit example shows that the fitting region can contain no middle point of target depth.
author: r132_reflected_fit
proof:
Convexity of \(C\) gives \((A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq A_1\). The height reflection \(h\mapsto2-h\) preserves depth and exchanges the endpoint bodies; it changes each height slope to its negative and leaves middle points and middle chords unchanged. Hence the chosen convention \(a_0=M\), \(a_2=m\) is legitimate.

For \(q\in\mathbb S^1\), use the cap functions of accepted fact `949ce2fdf2e1e240`, with its normal \(u\) renamed \(q\): \(G_i^q(c)=|A_i\cap\{w:q\cdot w\le c\}|\). A cut through \((1,p)\) with normal \(q\) and slope \(\lambda\) has endpoint thresholds \(c=q\cdot p+\lambda\) and \(2q\cdot p-c=q\cdot p-\lambda\). Varying \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\) is equivalent to varying \(c\in\mathbb R\). Thus

\[
\eta(p)=\inf_{q\in\mathbb S^1,\,c\in\mathbb R}
\bigl(G_0^q(c)+G_2^q(2q\cdot p-c)\bigr).
\tag{2}
\]

For every fixed \(q,p\), a sufficiently negative finite \(\lambda\) makes the height-zero cap empty and the height-two cap full. This follows from compactness and gives endpoint mass exactly \(m\), proving \(\eta(p)\le m\). Nonnegativity is immediate. The two horizontal halfspaces through \((1,p)\) have endpoint masses \(M\) and \(m\), so including them cannot lower (2). Any closed halfspace containing \((1,p)\) can be translated inward, parallel to its boundary, until that boundary passes through \((1,p)\). The resulting halfspace is contained in the original one and has no greater endpoint mass. This also proves the assertion about arbitrary containing halfspaces.

Fix \(p,q,c\), and reflect \(A_2\) about \(p\). Reflection preserves area and sends \(q\cdot w\le c\) to \(q\cdot a\ge2q\cdot p-c\). A line has planar area zero, so the closed boundaries give the exact identity

\[
G_0^q(c)+G_2^q(2q\cdot p-c)-m
=G_0^q(c)-|(2p-A_2)\cap\{w:q\cdot w\le c\}|.
\tag{3}
\]

If \(2p-A_2\subseteq A_0\), the right side of (3) is nonnegative for every \(q,c\). Together with (2) and \(\eta(p)\le m\), this proves \(\eta(p)=m\).

Conversely, suppose \(b\in(2p-A_2)\setminus A_0\). Strict separation of this point from the compact convex set \(A_0\) supplies a unit vector \(q\) and a number \(c\) such that \(q\cdot b<c<\min_{A_0}q\cdot w\). The \(A_0\) cap in (3) is therefore empty. The reflected cap in (3) has positive area: the reflected body is two-dimensional, and \(q\cdot b<c\); moving slightly from \(b\) toward an interior point gives an interior point still in this strict halfplane. Hence (3) is strictly negative, and (2) gives \(\eta(p)<m\). This proves both directions of (1), including touching containment and supporting-line cases. The factor \(2\) in (1) comes from the endpoint-threshold sum \(2q\cdot p\), not from an additional dilation.

Now suppose a row has \(e_j<m\), and take \(p\in\mathcal F\). If \(p\in Q_j\), then the halfspace
\(\{(h,w):q_j\cdot(w-p)+\lambda_j(h-1)\le0\}\)
passes through \((1,p)\) and is contained in \(\widehat H_j\), since \(q_j\cdot(p-z)\le0\). Its endpoint mass would be at most \(e_j<m=\eta(p)\), a contradiction. Thus \(q_j\cdot(p-z)>0\) for every \(p\in\mathcal F\). If all three payments were below \(m\), summing these strict inequalities with the positive weights would give \(0=\sum_j\alpha_jq_j\cdot(p-z)>0\). This proves the concurrent-cut consequence without any activity assumption.

Next assume the three rows are active at \((1,z)\). Their middle cap areas are \(|A_1\cap Q_j|=d-e_j\). For any row choose a finite slope

\[
\lambda'_j< -\max_{w\in A_0\cup A_2}\|w-z\|.
\tag{4}
\]

At height zero the new inequality is \(q_j\cdot(w-z)\le\lambda'_j\), which strictly excludes \(A_0\); at height two it is \(q_j\cdot(w-z)\le-\lambda'_j\), which strictly includes \(A_2\). The middle cap is unchanged. The new halfspace contains \((1,z)\), so its mass \(d-e_j+m\) is at least \(d\). Hence \(e_j\le m\). If \(e_j=m\), its new mass is exactly \(d\), and it remains an actual global minimum cut through \((1,z)\). The normal and all balancing weights remain unchanged.

We prove the chord bisection directly. The strict inequalities in (4) hold for every unit normal, so rotating the normal while keeping \(\lambda'_j\) fixed leaves both endpoint contributions constantly equal to \(0,m\). Let \(v\) be a unit vector perpendicular to \(q_j\), and write \(q_j(\theta)=q_j\cos\theta+v\sin\theta\). Let \(R(\phi)>0\) be the radial distance from \(z\) to \(\partial A_1\) in direction \(q_j\cos\phi+v\sin\phi\). Because \(z\in\operatorname{int}A_1\), this radial function is continuous. Polar integration gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Psi(\theta)
&:=|A_1\cap\{w:q_j(\theta)\cdot(w-z)\le0\}|\\
&=\frac12\int_{\theta+\pi/2}^{\theta+3\pi/2}R(\phi)^2\,d\phi,\\
\Psi'(0)&=\frac12\bigl(R(3\pi/2)^2-R(\pi/2)^2\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]

For every \(\theta\), the corresponding finite tail cut has mass \(m+\Psi(\theta)\ge d=m+\Psi(0)\). Therefore \(\Psi'(0)=0\), and the two positive radii in (5) are equal. The full middle chord has endpoints \(z+R(\pi/2)v\) and \(z-R(3\pi/2)v\), so its midpoint is \(z\). Its line depends only on \(q_j,z\), proving bisection also for the original row. This argument involves no selected outer edges or limiting slopes.

Assume now that every point of \(S\) has depth below \(t\). Accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e` gives \(a_i<T/2\) and \(a_1>M-m\). Together with compatibility and the absence of a middle point of depth \(t\), these satisfy the hypotheses of accepted fact `e4a8e2c026dd7346`. Hence an attained balanced active triple exists, with \(z\in\operatorname{int}A_1\) and \(0<d<t\).

Take any such triple. If \(\mathcal F\ne\varnothing\), the preceding arguments give at least one payment \(m\). There cannot be two. Otherwise relabel the payments as \(e,m,m\), with \(0\le e\le m\); the middle cap areas are \(d-e,d-m,d-m\), whose minimum is \(d-m\). Translate \(z\) to the origin and use the linear forms \(w\mapsto\alpha_jq_j\cdot w\). They are nonzero, pairwise nonparallel, and sum to zero, so the planar inequality of accepted fact `851e063a1b9908a3` applies to \(A_1-z\). It gives

\[
5(3d-e-2m)-6(d-m)\ge4a_1,
\qquad
9d\ge4a_1+5e+4m
\ge2T+2(a_1+m-M)>2T=9t.
\tag{6}
\]

This contradicts \(d<t\). Thus exactly one payment is \(m\), and the other two are below \(m\). The unique payment-\(m\) row has a bisected full middle chord by (5). If both other full middle chords were also bisected, the attained triple would satisfy every hypothesis of accepted fact `042183c313a2f323`, which gives a point of \(S\) of depth at least \(t\). This contradicts the assumed global failure, proving that at least one of the other two chords is off-center.

Finally consider \(A_0=A_1=\Delta\), \(A_2=\Delta/4\) from the statement. Their midpoint sum is \(5\Delta/8\subseteq\Delta\), so the convex hull of the three prescribed slices realizes exactly these three integer-height sections. Testing the three vertices of \(2p-\Delta/4\) against the three inequalities of \(\Delta\) gives exactly
\(\mathcal F=\{p=(p_x,p_y):p_x,p_y\ge1/8,\ p_x+p_y\le1/2\}\), which is nonempty. The areas are \(a_0=a_1=1/2\), \(m=1/32\), and \(t=11/48\). For every \(p\in\mathcal F\), the middle halfplane \(x+y\le p_x+p_y\) has cap area \((p_x+p_y)^2/2\le1/8\). Giving it a sufficiently negative finite height slope pays exactly \(m\) at the endpoints. Consequently
\(h_S((1,p))\le1/8+1/32=5/32<11/48=t\) for every \(p\in\mathcal F\). Thus the geometric fitting region can be disjoint from the middle target-depth region; its nonemptiness alone does not supply a target-depth point there.
statement:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^3\) be a compact polytope whose integer-height sections are exactly \(S=\bigcup_{i=0}^2(\{i\}\times A_i)\), with each \(A_i\) a compact two-dimensional convex polygon. Let \(\mu\) be the sum of planar area on these slices and \(h_S(y)=\inf\{\mu(H):H\text{ is a closed halfspace containing }y\}\). Retain \(a_i=|A_i|\), \(T=a_0+a_1+a_2\), \(M=\max\{a_0,a_2\}\), \(m=\min\{a_0,a_2\}\), and \(t=2T/9\). Reflect the height coordinate if necessary so that \(a_0=M\ge m=a_2>0\).

For a closed halfspace \(H\), write
\(\mu_{02}(H)=|\{w\in A_0:(0,w)\in H\}|+|\{w\in A_2:(2,w)\in H\}|\).
For \(p\in\mathbb R^2\), define its endpoint-only depth by

\[
\eta(p)=\inf_{q\in\mathbb S^1,\,\lambda\in\mathbb R}
\mu_{02}\bigl(\{(h,w):q\cdot(w-p)+\lambda(h-1)\le0\}\bigr).
\]

The point \(p\) and the function \(\eta\) are distinct from the full-measure middle maximizer \(z\) and its depth \(d\) below. For every \(p\in\mathbb R^2\),

\[
0\le\eta(p)\le m,
\qquad
\eta(p)=m\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 2p-A_2\subseteq A_0.
\tag{1}
\]

Including horizontal halfspaces, or allowing halfspaces that contain \((1,p)\) without requiring their boundary to pass through it, leaves \(\eta(p)\) unchanged. Put \(\mathcal F=\{p:2p-A_2\subseteq A_0\}\). The containment in (1) is in \(A_0\) itself; no planar depth region of \(A_0\) is required.

For any \(z\in\mathbb R^2\), consider three concurrent nonhorizontal cuts
\(\widehat H_j=\{(h,w):q_j\cdot(w-z)+\lambda_j(h-1)\le0\}\), where \(q_j\) are pairwise nonparallel unit vectors, \(\lambda_j\in\mathbb R\), and there are positive weights satisfying \(\sum_j\alpha_j=1\) and \(\sum_j\alpha_jq_j=0\). Define their middle halfplanes \(Q_j=\{w:q_j\cdot(w-z)\le0\}\) and actual endpoint payments \(e_j=\mu_{02}(\widehat H_j)\). Every row with \(e_j<m\) satisfies \(Q_j\cap\mathcal F=\varnothing\). Consequently, if \(\mathcal F\ne\varnothing\), these three payments cannot all be below \(m\).

Suppose, additionally, that these are attained active cuts at an interior middle maximizer:
\(z\in\operatorname{int}A_1\), \(d=h_S((1,z))=\max_{w\in A_1}h_S((1,w))\), and \(\mu(\widehat H_j)=d\) for every \(j\). Then \(0\le e_j\le m\). Every row with \(e_j=m\) can have its slope replaced by a finite slope that strictly excludes \(A_0\) and strictly includes \(A_2\), preserving its normal, middle halfplane, and full mass \(d\). Its full middle chord \(A_1\cap\partial Q_j\) is necessarily bisected by \(z\), including for the original slope.

If every point of \(S\) has depth below \(t\) and \(\mathcal F\ne\varnothing\), attained balanced active triples exist, and every such triple has exactly one payment equal to \(m\) and two payments below \(m\). Its unique payment-\(m\) row has the finite tail representative and bisected full middle chord just described. At least one of its other two full middle chords is not bisected by \(z\).

Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal F\) does not imply that any point \((1,p)\) with \(p\in\mathcal F\) meets the target depth: this fails for the compatible slices \(A_0=A_1=\Delta\), \(A_2=\Delta/4\), where \(\Delta=\{(x,y):x,y\ge0,\ x+y\le1\}\).
